To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
isoprene emission rates from the fast growing pioneer tree species V. guianensi increased with PAR up to 80 nmol m−2 s−1, and with leaf temperature (Topt,iso > 40 °C).

(1) isoprene emission from V. guineensis is high and not saturated with increasing photosynthetic photon flux density; (2) isoprene emissions and photosynthesis are uncoupled at high temperature; (3) methanol emission is high during leaf expansion; and (4) high ambient isoprene concentration are found above secondary Amazon forest.
isoprene and methylated emissions from the pioneer species Vismiaguianensis are high and that these emissions are regulated by light, temperature, leaf age, and leaf phenology.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the functional role of isoprenoids in tropical pioneer species and the implications of their emissions on the biogeochemical cycles of the Amazon forest and the atmospheric composition of the Amazon basin.
the role of isoprenes in plant defense and plant growth and how these roles are affected by environmental conditions.
the role of isoprenoids in the carbon balance of pioneer tree species in secondary tropical rainforests.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pioneer V. guianensi isoprenoid emissions are not only related to the growth rate of this pioneer species but also to its phenology and the environmental conditions in which it grows.
the allocation of carbon and energy to growth, defense, and maintenance varies with leaf ontogeny and is not constant throughout the life cycle of pioneer species.
isoprene emission rates are low in young leaves, and methanol emission rates are high in young leaves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

isoprene and methane emissions are not mutually exclusive, and the allocation of photosynthetic resources to isoprenoid emission is a function of plant phenology, environmental conditions, and leaf age.
